question: It's break time at magic school. Where do you go?

options.text: To the busy magic plaza to fly broomsticks with classmates
To a quiet corner of the library to read about magical creatures alone

question: Your professor assigns you to study a mysterious plant. What do you do first?

options.text: Carefully observe its leaf color, shape, and smell
Imagine what it could build if it grew huge, like a floating castle

question: Two young wizards are arguing over who gets to use a wand. How do you help?

options.text: Check the school rules to see whose wand it originally was, then decide fairly
Care about how they feel and suggest they take turns so no one is upset

question: Tomorrow you leave for the Mysterious Forest. What do you do tonight?

options.text: Neatly pack your potions, flashlight, and map in order
Feel too excited to plan — decide which path to take once you get there

question: At the magic feast, you need to introduce yourself. What do you do?

options.text: Walk right up, wave to everyone, and say lots of fun things
Feel a little shy and only want to chat with one or two close friends nearby

question: You find a glowing stone on the path. What's your first reaction?

options.text: Touch it to feel its texture, temperature, and weight
Wonder if it's a meteorite from space or holds ancient magic

question: You accidentally added the wrong ingredient and your potion changed color. What do you do?

options.text: Calmly think about what you added wrong and check a book to fix it
Feel upset, worried your professor will be disappointed or give you a low grade

question: You're in charge of the weekend magic show. What do you do?

options.text: Make a schedule ahead of time and assign who handles props and lines
Prepare as you go — improvising often brings the best surprises

question: Joining a new magic team, you usually...

options.text: Greet everyone right away and quickly become the group's happy spark
Quietly watch from the side and wait for others to talk to you first

question: During magic history class, what catches your attention most?

options.text: The exact years, places, and names of the heroes involved
The hidden meaning behind events, and how the world might change with different choices

question: Your best friend accidentally broke your crystal ball. What do you do?

options.text: Feel a bit sad, but since it was an accident, focus on figuring out how to fix it
First comfort your friend so they don't feel guilty, then deal with the broken ball

question: What does your desk or room usually look like?

options.text: Books and wands neatly arranged — I know exactly where everything is
A little messy, but I can always find my things — it feels more free that way

question: After a tiring day of magic training, how do you recharge?

options.text: Find some friends to chat, play cards, or games with
Go back to your room to listen to music or read a favorite picture book

question: If you could invent a brand new spell, you would choose to make:

options.text: A useful spell that quickly tidies your room or ties your shoes
A fantastical spell that lets you fly above the clouds into a rainbow castle

question: You just lost a game of magic chess. What's your first thought?

options.text: Figure out exactly which move went wrong so you can win next time
Feel a little sad, hoping your friend won't tease you for losing

question: Vacation is coming up. How do you plan for it?

options.text: Make a daily schedule and reading plan, and stick to it
No plans at all — sleep in and do whatever feels fun each day

question: You find an injured baby unicorn in the forest. What do you do?

options.text: Loudly call your friends for help while comforting the unicorn out loud
Quietly and gently approach, trying to softly pet it

question: While practicing broomstick flying, you prefer to:

options.text: Follow the standard posture your professor taught, step by step, to stay safe
Try figuring out your own flying tricks and new poses

question: During a team project, a teammate makes a mistake in the steps. You:

options.text: Point out the mistake directly, since fixing it quickly matters most for the team
Gently remind them, being careful to protect their confidence

question: Your professor gives homework with no deadline. You:

options.text: Finish it early so you can stop worrying about it
Set it aside and finish it all at once right before it's due
